Highest Analytically Implemented Derivative Order

Source: R/numerical_fallbacks.R
analytic_order.Rd

The largest \(k \le 4\) for which the link's own class registers a method for the order-\(k\) derivative generic; 0 when it registers none, so that only linkfun or linkinv is available.

Usage

analytic_order(x, inverse = FALSE)

Arguments

x

An object of class link.

inverse

Logical; TRUE to ask about the inverse-link generics.

Value

An integer between 0 and 4.

Details

Detection uses the documented S7 property that a method records the class it was registered on in its signature attribute: a method inherited from the base link class is a fallback, anything else is the link's own. Comparing method objects with identical() does not work for this, because S7 wraps them.

The recorded class is compared by name and package rather than with identical(), since identical() on S7 class objects tests object identity and returns FALSE for a class re-created from the same definition, as happens when the package's code is re-evaluated under coverage instrumentation; identity is kept only as a fast path.

The search stops at the first missing order, so the answer always means that every order up to it is analytic.

See also

link_fallback_orders, which reports this to the user.
